name: Artcell

global_influences.evidence: Band members have repeatedly cited Dream Theater (especially Images and Words and A Change of Seasons) as pivotal in shifting them toward progressive metal, odd time signatures, and technical playing. John Petrucci influenced Ershad's lead style; Mike Portnoy influenced Shaju's drumming.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Artcell page; Bass Musician Magazine interview with Cézanne (2021); Times of India interview (2007); official band materials

global_influences.evidence: Early underground shows featured Metallica covers. Lincoln cites Metallica as a school-era influence. Frequently listed among core influences.
Cited as a major influence on atmospheric and conceptual aspects. Cézanne (2007 interview) and other members reference Pink Floyd as among the biggest influences.
global_influences.source: Times of India interview; later secondary sources

global_influences.evidence: Sepultura and Pantera named as early heavy influences; Opeth cited by Cézanne for specific bass lines and later aesthetic direction.

local_adaptation_notes: Artcell consciously chose to write and perform in Bangla. Members have noted prior exposure to Bangladeshi folk, Rabindra Sangeet, Lalon, and Nazrul songs as a foundational layer that informs melodies and arrangements. Lyrics are noted for literary complexity and conceptual depth (early lyricist Rupok; later Ruman Ahmed and band members). The result is progressive metal that remains culturally grounded rather than a pure imitation of Western prog.
sound_evolution_summary: Early work (Onno Shomoy era): rawer progressive/heavy metal with strong guitar focus and technical ambition. Mid period (Oniket Prantor): increased melodic and atmospheric elements alongside complexity. Later work (Otritio and singles): further refinement of production, conceptual storytelling, and broader sonic experimentation while retaining progressive identity.
concert_culture_notes: Strong dedicated fan base; university and festival circuit historically important; large open-air and convention-centre shows in later years (e.g., Otritio open-air at ICCB). Also undertakes diaspora tours (Canada, Australia, etc.).
listener_community_notes: Attracts listeners seeking technical complexity, emotional depth, and literary Bangla lyrics. Forms a distinct node within the broader metal/prog ecosystem, with overlap to classic metal fans (Warfaze lineage) and alternative audiences.

sources.title: Cézanne – The Art of Bangladeshi Progressive Metal Bass (Bass Musician Magazine, 2021)
